messages:
anjali: Quick sync — before we lock the RFC, can we re-check tradeoffs between a regional shared gateway (our control plane -> customer VPC endpoint) vs a per-customer sidecar relay running in their VPC? I want to enumerate operational and security impacts.
max: Short answer: both valid. Longer: gateway = simpler ops + lower connection count on our side, sidecar = stronger isolation but higher mgmt.
maria: +1.  Key dimensions: connection scale, blast radius, cert/key management, cost (NAT/transit GW), deployment complexity, debugging.
sylvia: For AWS specifically: PrivateLink endpoints per-account get expensive at scale; TGW is complicated for cross-account. Sidecars avoid cross-account routing but add agents to customer infra.
anjali: Notes from last call: we worried about per-customer TLS tunnels overwhelming control plane sockets in hosted mode. Any numbers?
max: From the load spike sim: 10k customers with persistent tunnels -> ~100k concurrent connections (ssh/TCP) which increases file descriptors and memory on regional pods. Gateway model aggregates connections; we see ~5-10x reduction in connection churn.
maria: Security perspective: sidecar means keys and identity live on customer side; we treat them as zero-trust peers. Gateway model centralizes auth and creates a larger attacker surface if creds leaked. Need stronger rotation and short-lived tokens.
sylvia: Operationally, sidecar deployments mean we need a robust auto-updater and health checks. We also need tooling for logs/traces across hundreds of agents. That is non-trivial.
anjali: What about fallback behaviour? If gateway loses capacity, can we route to sidecar or vice-versa?
max: We could design a hybrid: default to gateway for small/medium customers, allow sidecar opt-in for high-security or high-throughput customers. Fallback path: gateway -> enqueue -> fallback to persistent sidecar connection if configured. Adds complexity to routing policy.
maria: Long-term refactor idea: abstract networking surface in control plane as a "transport plugin" with interfaces: connect(customer_id, svc, opts) -> returns connection handle; health(), metrics(). Implementations: privatelink-plugin, tgw-plugin, sidecar-plugin. That lets us iterate without big migrations.
sylvia: Agree. Also add cost-metering per-transport so sales can see $/month per-customer for endpoint infra.
anjali: Action items: 1) max spike to quantify fd/memory at 100k tunnels (due EOW) 2) maria + security to draft key rotation story for gateway (next Tue) 3) sylvia to sketch sidecar auto-update/installer constraints (PM/infra review). Anyone object?
max: sounds good. I'll kick off the load test and post results to #eng-infra.
maria: We'll run threat model for centralized gateway and doc mitigations.
infra-bot: Deployment alert: staging/gateway-proxy v0.12 rolled to us-east-1-demo at 2026-02-11T15:12:03Z :rocket:
anjali: Thanks all — we'll reconvene after spikes.
